question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}-8 \\ 9 \\ -17\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-8 \\ 9 \\ -17\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ -2{x}_{1} \\ 3{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2{x}_{2} \\ -3{x}_{2} \\ 5{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-8 \\ 9 \\ -17\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} \\ -2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-8 \\ 9 \\ -17\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=-8 \\ -2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} &=9 \\ 3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} &=-17\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Multiplying the first equation by $2$ and adding the result to the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} &=-7\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{2}=-7$ into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} &=9 \\ -2{x}_{1}-3(-7) &=9 \\ -2{x}_{1} &=-12 \\ {x}_{1} &=6\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=6$ and ${x}_{2}=-7$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} &=-17 \\ 3(6)+5(-7) &=-17 \\ -17 &=-17\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement.

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=6$ and ${x}_{2}=-7$, which means

$$
6{a}_{1}-7{a}_{2}=b.
$$

Consequently,

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=(6)+(-7)=-1.
$$
